newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat closes lower, hedges cited.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat closes lower, hedges cited.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures closed lower with hedge selling again cited as a key market factor, traders said.
"There was a little bit of country movement," a trader said. "The farmer's flat price near $4.00 is a psychological point that farmers want to sell."
Country Hedging was the chief seller of one million bushels of March, traders said. LFG Futures and Wilson Trading also sold roughly one half million bushels of March, they said.
Traders also said intermarket spreading was noted.
The spread volume wasn't heavy but Benson Quinn was featured buying MGE March and May with some of those purchases offset by sales in the CBOT and KCBT market.

The market was underpinned by talk this week India and Egypt were in the market for optional-origin wheat. Also there was some concern this week about dry weather in the U.S. Great Plains hard red winter wheat region. But there were some forecasts for rain early next week in key areas of the U.S. Plains hard red winter wheat growing region.
MGE spring wheat futures closed 1-3/4 to 4-1/2 cents per bushel lower, with March down three at $3.86-3/4.
